summary.headline: UBL Q1 FY27: EBITDA margin rose to 10.9% from 6.5% in Q4, but gross margin fell about 155 bps YoY to 41% amid a ~300 bps Middle East cost shock.
summary.overview: Sell-in volumes grew about 9% and sell-out volumes about 13%, in line with the industry, as UBL deliberately cut in-market inventory by about 20% YoY to protect cash flow. Reported gross margin was 41% (down ~155 bps YoY), with EBITDA margin at 10.9% and EBIT margin at 8%; the recovery programme recovered about half of the estimated ~300 bps hit. Premium margins turned accretive for the first time, with premium volumes up ~17% excluding intentional interventions. Management reiterated a double-digit revenue growth ambition for FY27 and flagged a Capital Markets Day in early September.

financial_highlights.change: YoY, dampened by contract brewer (CBU) source mix of ~4%

segments.name: Premium portfolio
segments.commentary: Premium margins became accretive for the first time; premium volumes up ~17% excluding intentional investment cuts in some markets. Kingfisher Ultra leads, and Heineken Silver grew ~28%. Premium is ~10-11% of revenue against a stated aspiration of ~20%.

segments.name: Contract brewers (CBU)
segments.commentary: CBU volumes grew ahead of overall volume, with an impact of ~4% on the quarter's reported revenue; the company reports contract brewing as one line, so inflation dampens reported revenue growth.

capex_capacity: Telangana can line commissioned; first can consumed in the week before the call (record commissioning time per management).
Two can lines added via brownfield expansion, one in Maharashtra and one in Telangana.
Greenfield brewery planned in Uttar Pradesh, where UBL currently uses a contract brewer; Karnataka has 2 UBL breweries that are now running full.
Punjab brewery closed; production transitioned to a partnership with ABB in Punjab, now complete.
Network optimisation completed in North Grid; more capacity planned in West Bengal in coming months to replace inter-state imports.
demand_pricing: Industry beer growth ~13% in the quarter; management says Karnataka category growth is 30-35% (over 50% in some recent months) after the ABV-based tax reform, with Maharashtra category growth above 20%.
Price increases implemented in 22 states, fully live by end of July; weighted pricing estimated at 2.5-3%, with further gains from price laddering and trade spend changes.
Trade discount cut in Haryana (product not sold at MRP), causing a significant volume drop there; West Bengal affected by stopping inter-state imports.
Brand power reported as improved for Kingfisher, Ultra and Heineken in April-June; Kingfisher Strong/Smooth innovation gaining share.
Maharashtra economy-segment growth seen; management says it is yet to be seen whether MML is affecting beer.
guidance_outlook: FY27 ambition: double-digit revenue growth with share gains, growing ahead of a high-single-digit category, and premium momentum.
Full-year war cost impact revised to the lower end of the INR 400-500 crore range, now estimated at INR 350-400 crore.
Management expects double-digit volume growth over the coming quarters, subject to no major policy roadblocks.
Gross margin is not guided quarter by quarter; management aims to expand margins over time, but would not call Q1 the bottom.
Inventory levels exiting December 2026 are not expected to fall YoY, as stock is built ahead of the peak season.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of contract brewers on price/mix, MML in Maharashtra, and FY27 ambition?
qa_highlights.answer: CBU volumes grew ahead of the total; reported revenue is dampened by a ~4% CBU impact. Underlying price/mix is ~+4%. MML impact is hard to see in data, but economy-segment growth in Maharashtra is affordability-driven. FY27 ambition remains double-digit revenue growth.

qa_highlights.question: Will the sell-in vs sell-out gap persist?
qa_highlights.answer: The gap was primarily a Q1 choice. Management expects sell-in and sell-through to converge, but will correct depot inventory where needed; inventory will not be materially lower exiting calendar 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin: has Q1 bottomed, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not guide quarter by quarter and would not commit that Q1 is the bottom. It expects margins to expand quarter over quarter over the longer term.

qa_highlights.question: Will volume growth return to double digits for the rest of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is building the plan for it and says data points to double-digit growth in the coming quarters, barring policy roadblocks.

qa_highlights.question: How much premium mix is needed to offset input inflation, and what is the premium share?
qa_highlights.answer: Premium scale alone offers limited offset given low beer margins; pricing and SKU-level revenue structure matter more. Premium is ~10-11% of revenue against a ~20% aspiration.

qa_highlights.question: Trade spend: is UBL responding to competitor aggression, and what happened in Haryana?
qa_highlights.answer: Trade spend was cut where state margins were thin, including Haryana, where the product is not sold at MRP. Management says it is not chasing business at any cost, and a balanced approach is taken with retailers, including coolers (50,000 placed) and faster claim settlement.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict cost volatility (packaging, logistics, FX, oil); management says visibility is low.
Ability to hold pricing in 22 states and whether volume growth recovers to double digits.
State policy stability (Karnataka, Maharashtra, UP) and negotiations on pricing and viability in some states.
Competitive trade-spend intensity from a large multinational player, and UBL's stance of not matching where state margins are thin.
Working capital (up ~38% YoY) and inventory normalisation ahead of the peak season.
Capital Markets Day in early September 2026 to be announced by email.
summary.management_tone: Confident on category growth and premium milestones, but cautious on the war and cost outlook ("we still are not out of the woods"). Management was open about trade-spend cuts and state-level volume weakness, and gave no firm quarterly margin guidance.
key_quotes: We're very happy with the cash flow delivery, where we also think it's really strengthening the muscle of generating profitable growth.
premium margins have become accretive for the first time in the past quarter.
We still are not out of the woods because of the war.
So over the longer term, we're still looking to expand margins, absolutely.

rows.label: Margin expansion

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Telangana can line already commissioned and Maharashtra brownfield can line added, with Karnataka's 2 breweries running full and West Bengal capacity planned in coming months.

rows.label: Volume growth

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Karnataka's 2 breweries are running full, a greenfield UP brewery is planned to replace a contract brewer, and more West Bengal capacity is planned, with a Capital Markets Day in early September as a likely venue.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held the double-digit revenue ambition and expects double-digit volume growth in coming quarters, but the cost outlook is still unclear and no quantified upgrade was given.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management still says 'not out of the woods' on the war cost outlook (visibility low), with the full-year impact only just cut to INR 350-400 crore from INR 400-500 crore and Q1 not called the margin bottom.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Kingfisher Strong/Smooth innovation is gaining share and premium volumes rose ~17%, but no specific new product launch dates were given.

rows.label: Price increases fully live in 22 states
rows.why: Price increases were implemented in 22 states and fully live by end of July, with weighted pricing estimated at 2.5-3% and underlying price/mix about +4% ex contract brewers.

rows.label: Inventory build ahead of peak season
rows.why: Working capital is up ~38% YoY and inventory exiting December 2026 is not expected to fall YoY, as stock is built for peak season, which may weigh on cash flow.

rows.label: Karnataka tax reform demand surge
rows.why: Karnataka category growth is 30-35% (over 50% in some recent months) after the ABV-based tax reform, and UBL's two Karnataka breweries are running full, so volume gains depend on the state policy holding.
